4 Mnth_BsMel   <NA>  0:0:0 1:0:0    +
5  Mnth_EdRd   <NA>  0:0:0 1:0:0    +

> timeshift_run <- timeShiftImages(inDir                = wd_images_raw,
+                                  timeShiftTable       = timeShift_Mnth,
+                                  stationCol           = "Station",
+                                  hasCameraFolders     = FALSE,
+                                  timeShiftColumn      = "timeshift",
+                                  timeShiftSignColumn  = "sign"
+ )
Error in `[<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, , i, value = c("Mnth_5DRLs", "Mnth_5DRRs",  :
  replacement has 6 rows, data has 0

Is this telling me my timeshiftTable does not match my directory and images?
The Station Names do match.  But are the images in the correct directory structure?
My images are in
ImagesCopy/Station1/SpeciesA/Img1, Img2
                     Station1/SpeciesB/Img10, Img11, Img22
                     ....
                     Station2/SpeciesA/Img1, Img2

When this did not work, I moved one lot of Species images to the Station. Thus
ImagesCopy/Station1/SpeciesA/
                                  /Img1, Img2
                                  /SpeciesB/Img10, Img11, Img22
I expected the function to process Img1, Img2

Yes I know I should not be using underscores in the Station Names but I have over 400 to change in image directories, DBs and GIS files..

Any suggestions, please, would be a big help.
Thanks David

messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

I am running all examples to understand the package. I have been trying both approaches: via drag and drop of images and metadata tagging (using digikam) but I am getting an error message. For example when I use checkSpeciesIdentification () and recordTable () functions:

> checkFolders <- checkSpeciesIdentification(inDir = directory_images_renamed,  IDfrom = "metadata", hasCameraFolders = F, maxDeltaTime = 120)

I obtain this message:

Error in checkSpeciesIdentification(inDir = directory_images_renamed,  :
  'metadataSpeciesTag' must be defined if IDfrom = 'metadata'

I used
> exifTagNames(directory_images_renamed, returnMetadata = T)

and I got metadata where tag for species seems to be recognized:

[69] "[XMP]           Tags List                       : Species/Agouti"
[70] "[XMP]           Last Keyword XMP                : Species/Agouti"
[71] "[XMP]           Hierarchical Subject            : Species|Agouti"
[72] "[XMP]           Catalog Sets                    : Species|Agouti"
[73] "[XMP]           Subject

In addition, I noted something: Vignette says "To update the image metadata with your new tag structure (and to populate the image metadata tag “HierarchicalSubject” that camtrapR reads), select the images, click the “More” button in the bottom right corner of the screen, then “Write metadata to each file”." But I did not see the button Write metadata to each file, active (I attache image file).

I do not know what I am doing wrong. I hope you can help me.

Best,

messages.subject: Re: problems with metadata
messages.body_plain:
Dear Angela,
my apologies for the late reply.

The error message tells you that the argument 'metadataSpeciesTag' must be defined if you use metadata tags for species ID. In your example, it would be

checkFolders <- checkSpeciesIdentification(inDir = directory_images_renamed,  IDfrom = "metadata", hasCameraFolders = F, maxDeltaTime = 120, metadataSpeciesTag = "Species")

About writing the metadata tags to images, did you select the images that you wish to write the metadata tags into? The button should be available if images are selected.
Please let me know if this doesn't work.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: output exifTagNames ( )
messages.body_plain:
Yes, this is normal and expected, but can be confusing.

exifTagNames(..., returnMetadata = T) returns the contents of metadata tags. This is to assess which metadata tags are relevant, as they may partly be manufacturer-specific.The names of the metadata tags are different from the ones returned when exifTagNames(..., returnMetadata = F). In the former, they may contain spaces etc., but not in the latter. Use the metadata tag names returned by exifTagNames(..., returnMetadata = F) in the record table functions (in the additionalMetadataTags argument).

Please also have a look here in the vignette:
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/DataExtraction.html#extracting-image-metadata

messages.subject: Re: Image Management software and Tag Structure
messages.subject_clean: Image Management software and Tag Structure
messages.body_plain:
Hi Marcelo,
i never used Mediapro, so I don't know if it works.

Nevertheless, here are some suggestions:

Uncheck the check box to make the software embed the metadata (this is what digikam does too).
Tag a few sample images and try to run the functions you wish to run (try recordTable() and exifTagNames()). If you get the desired output, fine. But as you supposed, there is a bit more to the process that is happening under the hood. Most importantly, digikam writes the tags into a tag called "
HierarchicalSubject". The content of this tag looks something like this: "Species|Black Bear, individual|1".  (for Species = Black Bear and individual 1).
So, if Mediapro writes the tag into the HierachicalSubject tag and separates the tag name and tag value by either "|" or ".", you it should work. If it is ".", read up on the argument metadataHierarchyDelimitor in the recordTable functions.

About your second question regarding the tag structure, you got it right. Option1 will not work, but option 2 will.

Please let me know if Mediapro wirks for you.
Best regards,
Jürgen
